prompts.label: IMAGE PIPELINE
prompts.placeholder: What are the major stages of an image pipeline?

prompts.label: WHY PIPELINE IMAGES?
prompts.placeholder: What operational problem does Image Builder solve?

reveal.text: EC2 Image Builder automates repeatable image creation, testing, patching, and distribution so fleets can launch from controlled images instead of hand-maintained servers.

prompts.label: WHAT DOES ECR STORE?
prompts.placeholder: What artifact is ECR designed to manage?

reveal.text: Amazon ECR is a managed container image registry. It stores and distributes container images and integrates with AWS identity, scanning, lifecycle, and deployment workflows.

prompts.label: OPERATE THE REGISTRY
prompts.placeholder: Reveal one operational control at a time.

cells.purpose: Identify known package/image vulnerabilities according to the configured scanning capability.
Expire old or unneeded images to control registry growth.
Control who can pull, push, or manage repository content.

prompts.label: STACK MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: What does CloudFormation manage?

reveal.text: A CloudFormation template declares AWS resources and relationships; a stack is the deployed instance of that template. CloudFormation tracks the resources it manages and applies changes to move the stack toward the template.

prompts.label: INSPECT A TEMPLATE
prompts.placeholder: Click the structural fields that CloudFormation uses to build this stack.

reveal.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Parameters:
  BucketName:
    Type: String
Resources:
  AppBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Ref BucketName
Outputs:
  BucketArn:
    Value: !GetAtt AppBucket.Arn

annotations.title: Template parameters
annotations.explanation: Parameters let callers supply values without editing the template.

annotations.title: Managed resources
annotations.explanation: Resources declares the AWS objects CloudFormation should manage.

annotations.title: Reference
annotations.explanation: !Ref reads another template value and creates the necessary dependency/value relationship.

annotations.title: Resource attribute
annotations.explanation: !GetAtt reads an attribute produced by a managed resource.

prompts.label: FROM CDK CODE TO STACK
prompts.placeholder: How does CDK reach CloudFormation?

items: Write infrastructure in a supported programming language
CDK constructs build an application model

prompts.label: CDK DOES NOT BYPASS CLOUDFORMATION
prompts.placeholder: What executes the infrastructure change?

reveal.text: CDK synthesizes CloudFormation templates. CloudFormation remains the deployment engine for the resulting stacks.

prompts.label: CHANGE SET OR DRIFT DETECTION?
prompts.placeholder: Reveal one operational question at a time.

cells.need: What would this template update change?
Has a managed resource changed outside CloudFormation?
cells.answer: Differences between expected stack configuration and supported actual resource properties.

prompts.label: INSPECT A NESTED STACK
prompts.placeholder: Click the fields that make one stack call another template.

reveal.code:
Resources:
  Network:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
    Properties:
      TemplateURL: https://example-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/network.yaml
      Parameters:
        Environment: prod

annotations.title: Nested stack resource
annotations.explanation: A nested stack is represented as an AWS::CloudFormation::Stack resource inside the parent template.

annotations.title: Child template location
annotations.explanation: TemplateURL points to the child template that the nested stack deploys.

annotations.title: Pass values to the child
annotations.explanation: Parameters pass values from the parent stack into the child template.

prompts.label: WHEN NESTED STACKS FIT
prompts.placeholder: What problem do nested stacks solve?

reveal.text: Nested stacks let you compose a larger stack from reusable template components while keeping a parent-child deployment relationship.

prompts.label: UNDERSTAND STACKSETS
prompts.placeholder: Reveal each dimension of a StackSet rollout.

cells.meaning: How StackSets obtains authority to deploy across target accounts.
How concurrency and failure tolerance are controlled during rollout.

prompts.label: INSPECT RESOURCE RETENTION
prompts.placeholder: Click the two policies and distinguish stack deletion from replacement.

reveal.code:
Resources:
  Database:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    DeletionPolicy: Snapshot
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Snapshot
    Properties:
      DBInstanceClass: db.t3.micro

annotations.title: Stack deletion behavior
annotations.explanation: DeletionPolicy controls what CloudFormation does with the resource when the resource is removed from the stack or the stack is deleted, subject to service/policy semantics.

annotations.title: Replacement behavior
annotations.explanation: UpdateReplacePolicy controls what CloudFormation does with the old physical resource when an update requires replacement.

prompts.label: TROUBLESHOOT A FAILED STACK
prompts.placeholder: Reveal the evidence source that answers each question.

cells.question: Which resource failed first?
cells.why: Shows resource-level status transitions and failure messages.

cells.question: Could the target subnet/AZ satisfy the request?
cells.why: Some failures are placement or capacity constraints rather than template syntax.

prompts.label: WHY VERSION IAC?
prompts.placeholder: What changes when infrastructure definitions live in source control?

reveal.text: Version control gives infrastructure changes history, review, collaboration, rollback context, and a repeatable source of intent instead of undocumented console changes.

prompts.label: SAFE CHANGE FLOW
prompts.placeholder: What is a useful change workflow?

prompts.label: TERRAFORM MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: What are the main pieces?

reveal.text: Terraform Core reads configuration, builds a dependency graph, works with providers, compares desired configuration with state and remote objects, then plans and applies changes.

prompts.label: INSPECT A TERRAFORM CONFIG
prompts.placeholder: Click the important HCL structures.

annotations.title: Provider source
annotations.explanation: The source address identifies the provider package Terraform should install.

annotations.title: Provider version constraint
annotations.explanation: The version constraint limits acceptable provider versions.

annotations.title: Provider configuration
annotations.explanation: The provider block configures how Terraform talks to AWS.

annotations.title: Managed resource
annotations.explanation: A resource block declares an object Terraform should manage.

prompts.label: CHOOSE A DEPLOYMENT APPROACH
prompts.placeholder: Reveal one approach at a time.

cells.fit: Lower-complexity changes where rollback/replacement risk is acceptable.

cells.risk: Keeps old and new environments separate during cutover
cells.fit: Safer cutover/rollback when duplicate capacity is acceptable.

cells.risk: Exposes only a small portion of traffic/capacity first
cells.fit: Changes where early signal can validate the new version before broad rollout.

prompts.label: MATCH THE SYSTEMS MANAGER TOOL
prompts.placeholder: Reveal one operational job at a time.

cells.job: Run a command on managed nodes
Keep node configuration in a desired state
Interactive managed shell without opening inbound SSH/RDP

prompts.label: INSPECT A COMMAND DOCUMENT
prompts.placeholder: Click the fields that tell SSM what to run.

reveal.code:
schemaVersion: '2.2'
description: Check disk usage
mainSteps:
  - action: aws:runShellScript
    name: checkDisk
    inputs:
      runCommand:
        - df -h

annotations.title: Command document schema
annotations.explanation: Command documents commonly use the 2.2 schema for managed-node command execution.

annotations.title: Plugin/action
annotations.explanation: aws:runShellScript executes shell commands on supported managed nodes.

annotations.title: Command payload
annotations.explanation: runCommand contains the actual command lines sent to the managed node.

prompts.label: WHY IT SCALES BETTER THAN SSH
prompts.placeholder: What operational advantage does Run Command provide?

reveal.text: Run Command can target managed nodes by IDs or tags and run commands without requiring operators to open inbound administrative ports or manually connect to each server.

prompts.label: PATCH OR DESIRED STATE?
prompts.placeholder: Reveal one feature at a time.

cells.example: Apply approved security patches during a maintenance period.

cells.goal: Maintain a desired configuration on managed nodes
cells.example: Ensure an agent/configuration remains installed and configured.

prompts.label: SCHEDULE OR CONNECT?
prompts.placeholder: Separate the two operational jobs.

columns.title: Maintenance Windows
items: Useful for patching/commands/automation at approved times

columns.title: Session Manager
items: Interactive shell access to managed nodes

prompts.label: WHAT MAKES AUTOMATION DIFFERENT?
prompts.placeholder: Why not just use Run Command for everything?

reveal.text: Automation coordinates a sequence of runbook steps and can call AWS APIs, branch, wait, invoke other automation, and manage remediation workflows beyond a single node command.

prompts.label: AUTOMATION FLOW
prompts.placeholder: How should you think through a remediation runbook?

prompts.label: INSPECT THE MATCH
prompts.placeholder: Click the fields that make this an EC2 termination event pattern.

annotations.title: Source filter
annotations.explanation: Matches events from the EC2 service.

annotations.title: Event type
annotations.explanation: Matches EC2 instance state-change notifications.

annotations.title: Specific state
annotations.explanation: Narrows the pattern to the terminated state.

prompts.label: RULES NEED TARGETS
prompts.placeholder: What happens after a match?

reveal.text: A matching EventBridge rule routes the event to configured targets such as Lambda, SNS, Step Functions, Systems Manager, or supported AWS service/API targets.

prompts.label: INSPECT A SMALL REMEDIATION
prompts.placeholder: Click the AWS SDK calls to see the control flow.

annotations.title: Service client
annotations.explanation: The Lambda function uses the AWS SDK client to call EC2 APIs.

annotations.title: Event input
annotations.explanation: The function reads the resource identifier from the event payload.

annotations.title: Remediation API
annotations.explanation: The function performs the intended AWS API action; its IAM role must allow that action on the intended scope.

prompts.label: CHOOSE AN S3 EVENT DESTINATION
prompts.placeholder: Reveal one destination pattern at a time.

cells.fit: Fan out object-event notifications to subscribers.
Buffer object-event work for asynchronous consumers.
Run code directly in response to object events.
Use richer event routing and integration patterns.

prompts.label: FILTER EARLY
prompts.placeholder: Why use prefix/suffix filters where supported?

reveal.text: Filtering object-event notifications reduces unnecessary downstream invocations by limiting events to the object keys that the workflow actually cares about.
